name: Battery: second or subsequent offense
conductSummary: Committing battery after a prior conviction for battery, aggravated battery, felony battery, or resisting an officer with violence. The prior-conviction definition includes withheld adjudication and a nolo contendere plea. The underlying battery conduct is an intentional unwanted touch or strike, or intentionally causing bodily harm.
additionalPenalty: The resisting-with-violence prior-conviction alternative was added effective July 1, 2026; earlier conduct requires the earlier statutory version. Section 741.2801(3) expressly excludes this section 784.03(2) felony battery from its domestic-violence repeat enhancement.
namingBasis: Source-derived offense name with a descriptive branch qualifier; qualifier is not claimed to be a statutory short title.

name: Felony battery
conductSummary: Actually and intentionally touching or striking another person against that person's will and causing great bodily harm, permanent disability, or permanent disfigurement.
additionalPenalty: For conduct on or after July 1, 2026, if this is a crime of domestic violence within section 741.28 and the accused had a prior domestic-violence conviction when the offense occurred, section 741.2801 reclassifies it to a second-degree felony, ordinarily punishable by up to 15 years imprisonment and a conventional fine up to $10,000. That conviction definition includes withheld adjudication and a nolo contendere plea. A dating relationship alone does not establish the family-or-household relationship required by section 741.28.
namingBasis: Source-derived offense name with a descriptive branch qualifier; qualifier is not claimed to be a statutory short title.

name: Domestic battery by strangulation
conductSummary: Knowingly and intentionally impeding the breathing or blood circulation of a family or household member or a person in a continuing significant romantic or intimate relationship, against that person's will, by pressure on the throat or neck or blocking the nose or mouth, creating a risk of or causing great bodily harm. Authorized medical diagnosis, treatment, or prescription is excluded. Family or household membership uses section 741.28, including its residence qualification and shared-child exception.
additionalPenalty: For conduct on or after July 1, 2026, if this is a crime of domestic violence within section 741.28 and the accused had a prior domestic-violence conviction when the offense occurred, section 741.2801 reclassifies it to a second-degree felony, ordinarily punishable by up to 15 years imprisonment and a conventional fine up to $10,000. name: Aggravated stalking: after an injunction or court prohibition
conductSummary: Knowingly, willfully, maliciously, and repeatedly following, harassing, or cyberstalking another person after one of the listed protective injunctions or another court-imposed prohibition concerning that person or their property. The statutory definitions require the specified course of conduct and exclude constitutionally protected activity; credible-threat stalking is a separately covered branch.
additionalPenalty: Section 784.048(8) requires punishment to run consecutively to a former sentence for the listed offenses. Under subsection (9), the court must consider a no-contact order that may last up to 10 years. For conduct on or after July 1, 2026, if this is a crime of domestic violence within section 741.28 and the accused had a prior domestic-violence conviction when the offense occurred, section 741.2801 reclassifies it to a second-degree felony, ordinarily punishable by up to 15 years imprisonment and a conventional fine up to $10,000. name: Aggravated battery: victim age 65 or older
conductSummary: The underlying aggravated battery involves intentional or knowing great bodily harm, permanent disability or disfigurement, use of a deadly weapon, or battery on a person known or reasonably understood to be pregnant. Section 784.08 reclassifies it when the victim is 65 or older, regardless of whether the accused knew or had reason to know the victim's age.
additionalPenalty: Section 784.08(1) requires a minimum of 3 years imprisonment, a fine not exceeding $10,000, restitution, and up to 500 hours of community service in addition to punishment. Adjudication of guilt or imposition of sentence may not be suspended, deferred, or withheld under section 784.08(3). For conduct on or after July 1, 2026, if this is a crime of domestic violence within section 741.28 and the accused had a prior domestic-violence conviction when the offense occurred, section 741.2801 reclassifies it to a life felony, ordinarily punishable by imprisonment for life and a conventional fine up to $15,000. That conviction definition includes withheld adjudication and a nolo contendere plea. A dating relationship alone does not establish the family-or-household relationship required by section 741.28.
